subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should OpenClaw change managed plugin npm roots to stop propagating broad host overrides like path-to-regexp into third-party plugin dependency graphs, or only add diagnostics for known incompatible plugin stacks?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix changes the plugin dependency ownership and security-override boundary, which repository policy treats as compatibility and product-sensitive.

options.title: Scoped managed-root policy
options.body: Stop applying incompatible broad host overrides to plugin-owned dependency graphs while preserving OpenClaw-owned dependency and security policy, with tests for Express 4 and Express 5 plugin installs.

options.title: Validator and diagnostic only
options.body: Keep current override propagation but detect Express 4/path-to-regexp conflicts during plugin install or doctor and emit a clear repair hint.

options.title: Plugin-local ownership only
options.body: Leave core unchanged and require affected plugin packages to publish their own shrinkwrap or override until they migrate away from Express 4.

recommendation.title: Scoped managed-root policy
recommendation.body: Stop applying incompatible broad host overrides to plugin-owned dependency graphs while preserving OpenClaw-owned dependency and security policy, with tests for Express 4 and Express 5 plugin installs.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly connected in current history to managed npm override propagation and plugin dependency-root behavior.
